newsitem.title: HONG KONG: BA to move ex-HK cargo flights to Stansted May 17.
newsitem.headline: BA to move ex-HK cargo flights to Stansted May 17.

text.p: HONG KONG, May 13 - (Reuter) British Airways will transfer its three weekly cargo flights between Hong Kong and London Gatwick to London Stansted from May 17, BA World Cargo Greater China regional manager Chris Chan said.
"Gatwick is too congested and we reckon Stansted is more efficient to handle freighters. Our customers will see an improvement in service," Chan told Reuters.
An overnight trucking operation will link Stansted airport in Essex with BA's Heathrow home base, along with Gatwick, Birmingham, Manchester, Glasgow and Dublin airports.

"We are also trying to relieve pressure from our main Heathrow hub so these designated trucks purely for Hong Kong freight will quickly link up with our other hubs such as Birmingham and Manchester," Chan added.

BA's 100-tonne capacity Boeing 747-200 freighter, wet-leased from cargo specialist airline Atlas Air, leaves Hong Kong on Monday, Thursday and Saturday mornings and is due to arrive at Stansted later the same day.
After unloading and cargo breakdown, the first truck is due to leave 30 minutes after landing, with the entire aircraft load dispatched within two hours, Chan said.
Freight forwarders in Hong Kong contacted by Reuters said they had not yet been told about the imminent switch of airports and were surprised at the suddenness of the move.
"This is the first I have heard of it and it is very short notice. Hopefully the move to Stansted will help because BA Cargo has had a reputation for bad service for a long time," said one.
Industry observers said the cargo switch to Stansted will free more slots for BA passenger flights at Gatwick.

They added that a proposed link-up between BA and American Airlines is dependent, among other factors, on BA acceding to a demand from the British Office of Fair Trading to give up slots at Heathrow to make way for new competition.
